messages:
marta-sales: FYI TelComX POC kickoff scheduled for next Wed. They require strict in-country residency for request payloads and logs (Country Z). No subprocessors operating in Country Z allowed. They also want hosted API to act as a fallback only if we can guarantee no PII leaves Country Z — otherwise fallback must be disabled. Asking for delta on pricing for a 1-month dedicated reserved pool + egress credit.

devon-solutions: Understood. Do they want VPC peering + private control plane, or an air-gapped on-prem?

marta-sales: Prefer VPC peering for primary; hosted as secondary. Security flagged "no subprocessors in Country Z" as a strict clause.

liam-ops: We can deploy private nodes in Country Z and configure VPC peering. Caveat: our standard observability/metrics exporters live in Region Y. Two options: (A) customer-managed observability forwarder running in their VPC that ships only aggregated metrics to in-country SIEM, (B) enable air-gapped collector that writes to local storage and customer ingests. Option A is quicker.

sasha-security: Quick notes: (1) KMS BYOK supported — need CMK ARN + access policy. (2) Mutual TLS required for peering. (3) Observability: if they forbid any external agents in Country Z then forwarder must be customer-controlled with no external telemetry. (4) Subprocessor restriction: we can blacklist subprocessors in Country Z for control and telemetry paths, but some infra providers (CDN, cert issuers) may still transit outside; we need to document and get legal signoff.

marta-sales: They explicitly disallow vendor processes running in Country Z, not cross-border telemetry if the telemetry endpoint is their in-country SIEM. So forwarder -> SIEM in Country Z is acceptable if forwarder is customer-managed.

devon-solutions: I'll draft a minimal checklist for their infra: 1) VPC peering CIDRs + route table examples; 2) mTLS cert exchange steps; 3) BYOK/KMS instructions; 4) observability forwarder container image, ports, env vars; 5) header gating for fallback (see below); 6) smoke test endpoints + sample curl.

liam-ops: On fallback gating: we should require a signed tenant consent header to enable cross-border fallback. Suggested header: X-Redwood-Fallback-Consent: signed=<base64-sig>. Without it, our router must reject requests that would exit Country Z. This prevents accidental PII egress.

sasha-security: Agreed. Also add an API policy: if request contains pii=true and no signed consent, return 403 with code RESIDENCY_BLOCKED. We'll provide a small middleware snippet for their devs.

marta-sales: Pricing question from TelComX: what's the delta for a month-long dedicated reserved pool vs hosted with fallback?

devon-solutions: Ballpark: dedicated reserved pool (approx 1 A100-equivalent sustained) ~ $55k-70k/month depending on commitment and support SLAs. Hosted fallback billed at standard hosted token rates; egress credit can be negotiated — e.g., up to 100M tokens with 25-35% discount on egress within committed window. Need presales to finalize exact quote.

liam-ops: Ops item: if fallback allowed, we must ensure PII never leaves Country Z without consent. That signed header approach covers it, but we also need runtime enforcement in the routing layer and a log/alert whenever fallback is used so TelComX can audit.

sasha-security: I'll produce an exportable subprocessor inventory (redacted IPs/regions) and a short security checklist. Legal will need to sign a Subprocessor Commitment Amendment to guarantee we won't run subprocessors in Country Z.

legal-bot: Reminder: any amendment must include term length, scope (control plane, telemetry, infra), and liability/indemnity clauses. Presales to draft and Legal to review — target 72h turnaround.

marta-sales: Action items: devon -> 1-page infra checklist + routing policy snippet; liam -> confirm observability deployment options and runtime gating implementation; sasha -> subprocessor inventory + security checklist; legal-bot -> prepare amendment draft. I'll coordinate TelComX security contact tomorrow. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Provisioning ticket created: PROV-9081. Staging peering test scheduled tues-1400 UTC.

marta-sales: Thanks all. I'll update the customer and push the security questionnaire answers tonight.
